reasons: Lake record is verified with record_id/input_case_name Peters v. New York, U.S. Supreme Court, date_decided 1968-06-10, and year 1968.
Official citation 392 U.S. 40, vendor citation 1968 U.S. LEXIS 1346, and parallel cites 88 S. Ct. 1889, 20 L. Ed. 2d 917, and 44 Ohio Op. 2d 402 match the lake record.
residual_risks: Lake canonical case_name is Sibron v. New York and canonical_name_match is false, so the Peters page should continue to signal that it is the Peters component of the consolidated Sibron/Peters opinion.
reviewed.suggested_tightening: Keep the citation display tied to the qualifier "decided with Sibron v. New York" to avoid caption ambiguity.

reasons: The opinion states that by the time Officer Lasky caught Peters between the fourth and fifth floors, he had probable cause to arrest for attempted burglary.
The opinion states that when Lasky grabbed Peters by the collar he seized him on probable cause, had authority to search Peters, and that the incident search was justified.
residual_risks: The holding is compressed; the probable-cause basis was not bare flight alone, but flight plus strange noises, unfamiliar men, tiptoeing, continued maneuvers, and the officer's burglary inference.
reviewed.suggested_tightening: Specify that furtive conduct and flight were coupled with Officer Lasky's specific observations suggesting attempted burglary.

reasons: The opinion expressly treats the search as properly incident to a lawful arrest and says Lasky had authority to search once Peters was seized on probable cause.
That directly supports placement on SIA Persons, at least as a related cross-doctrine authority.
residual_risks: The role may understate the case's usefulness for search-incident doctrine, but it is not overclaimed.
reviewed.suggested_tightening: Consider a stronger SIA role if the corpus taxonomy distinguishes direct search-incident authorities from merely related cases.

reasons: The opinion identifies Peters/Sibron as companion cases to Terry and discusses New York's stop-and-frisk statute.
The Court explains that Peters was justified by probable cause and search incident to arrest rather than by a less-than-probable-cause Terry-style frisk, supporting a related cross-doctrine role.
residual_risks: Peters is more useful as a boundary case than as a core Terry-stop rule.
reviewed.suggested_tightening: Label it as a probable-cause/search-incident boundary case if the home page supports such roles.
